about: Every creature record of the game's masters and what this build does with it. tools/creature_census.py reads it on every build (the image step, after the NPC gallery catalogue): a creature record is built when the image places it (the maps and the actor table); one that is not built takes the first group below whose fact holds for it (expansion: defined by a master the image does not read; summon: named by a game setting sMagic...ID, the creature a summoning effect calls up; interior: placed in rooms only; unused: no placement, used levelled list, script, dialogue result or summoning setting names it), and a placement of a built creature in a room that the room stage does not place is counted under the interior group. A group is missing (with the register entry that tracks it) or skipped (on purpose, with its reason). A record that is not built and that no group names, and a levelled creature point of the base master that is not placed in a cell no levelled_points group names stop a full build, so a creature is never left out silently. The facts no_model (no MODL or a mesh the data lacks), left_out (the actor library refused the mesh) and script (placed by a script only) have no group today: a record with them stops the build until it is registered and a group is added.

groups.name: Not used by the game data
groups.reason: No placement, used levelled list, script, dialogue result or summoning setting of the masters names these records (unused variants: dead bodies with no placement, quest creatures the game never places, duplicates of placed ones); there is nothing to show.

levelled_points.name: Levelled creatures in the intro scene's rooms
levelled_points.reason: The intro scene stage converts these rooms with the older room path, which lists a levelled creature reference as left out; only the room stages write the rooms' levelled creature points (tools/room_levelled.py).
